subject.title: fix(cli-runner): sweep orphaned bundle MCP temp dirs at gateway startup

question: Should gateway startup deliberately retain all legacy pre-ownership bundled-MCP temp directories for manual cleanup in order to guarantee rolling-upgrade safety?
rationale: The branch resolves the unsafe heuristic by never deleting an unprovable legacy directory, but that deliberately retains prior credential-bearing leaks until an operator stops the gateway and removes them.

options.title: Accept the safety tradeoff
options.body: Merge with legacy directories retained and document the explicit operator cleanup path after a rolling upgrade.

options.title: Pause for a migration design
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers choose a separately safe migration or cleanup mechanism for legacy directories.

recommendation.title: Accept the safety tradeoff
recommendation.body: Merge with legacy directories retained and document the explicit operator cleanup path after a rolling upgrade.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the production reproduction and the concrete compatibility analysis, making them the best available routing contact while repository ownership history remains unverified.
